title: SRE Standards: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives, Incident Review Standards, and Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
body:
Overview

This document defines Redwood Inference engineering standards for Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning guidance, reliability initiatives, incident review standards, operational tooling expectations, and a canonical SRE runbook template. It is intended for service owners, SREs, and on-call engineers who operate production inference services.

Goals
- Provide a consistent SLO / error budget framework across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Standardize capacity planning to reduce outages caused by resource starvation.
- Define a blameless incident review process and postmortem requirements.
- Centralize operational tooling and runbooks for faster incident mitigation and knowledge transfer.

Scope
- Applies to all production-facing services under Redwood control (API gateway, inference runtime, batching service, cache, monitoring/ingestion pipelines).
- Does not replace service-specific runbooks — each service must publish its SLOs and runbooks in the centralized runbook repository.

1) SLO & Error Budget Framework

Principles
- SLOs should reflect user-facing experience (latency, availability, correctness) and be measurable from production telemetry.
- Use one primary SLO per customer-facing flow and a small set of secondary SLOs for internal invariants.
- Error budgets are the operational currency that informs rollouts, capacity, and mitigations.

Definitions
- SLI (Service Level Indicator): The metric that quantifies user experience (e.g., p99 inference latency, successful-response ratio).
- SLO: The target for an SLI over a measurement window (e.g., 99.95% availability over 30 days).
- Error budget: 1 - SLO; the allowed fraction of bad events in the window.
- Measurement window: Rolling window used for SLO evaluation (standard: 30d).

Standard SLO Types and Examples
| SLO name | SLI source | Target | Measurement window | Alert threshold | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| API availability (hosted API) | 5xx response ratio from API gateway (Datadog) | 99.95% | 30d rolling | 99.9% (7d rolling drop) | api-team@redwood.internal |
| Inference p99 latency (text-gen) | p99 end-to-end latency (tracing + metrics) | <= 600ms | 30d rolling | p99 > 700ms sustained 1h | runtime-team@redwood.internal |
| Embeddings throughput | requests/sec processed (ingest metrics) | sustain 5k rps cluster-wide | 30d rolling | sustained < 4k rps for 2h | infra-team@redwood.internal |
| Model correctness (rerank accuracy) | regression eval score on production prompt-set | >= 93% | 30d rolling | < 92% for 24h | applied-ml@redwood.internal |

SLI Instrumentation and Sources
- Primary telemetry: Datadog metrics + tracing (OpenTelemetry spans). Secondary sources: Prometheus (internal infra), ELK for logs, model eval harness for correctness.
- SLI definition must include: metric name, dimensions (route, model-version, region), aggregation method, and sampling bias notes.
- All SLOs must be published to the SLO registry (GitHub repo: infra/slo-registry) with a link from the Confluence SLO page.

SLO Lifecycle and Ownership
- Each service owner declares the SLO(s) and the owner contact. SRE reviews and approves on a quarterly cadence.
- Changes to SLOs require: (1) proposal PR in infra/slo-registry, (2) SRE review, (3) 2-week trial monitoring period, (4) merge and Confluence update.

Error Budget Burn & Policy
- Conservatively classify burn: planned releases, experiments, and capacity constraints should be accounted separately.
- Burn rate policies (examples):
  - Green (safe): remaining error budget >= 50% — normal rollouts allowed.
  - Yellow (watch): remaining error budget between 25% and 50% — slower rollouts, increased monitoring, notify product/exec if rollouts continue.
  - Red (stop): remaining error budget < 25% — halt non-essential rollouts, trigger incident review, request mitigation plan from owner.
- Automated actions: when burn rate triggers Yellow/Red thresholds, the SLO monitoring automation will open a ticket in JIRA and notify the on-call channel.

2) Capacity Planning Guidance

Objectives
- Ensure headroom to meet SLOs during expected peaks (traffic spikes, regional failovers, batch replays).
- Define clear ramp policies for model rollouts and major customer onboarding.

Processes and Cadence
- Quarterly capacity review: infra team publishes capacity dashboard (GPU count, slots, reserved pools, avg utilization) and a 90-day forecast.
- Monthly safety buffer check: ensure free capacity >= 25% for hosted fleet (region-specific). For Dedicated pools, ensure contractual headroom per customer SLA.
- Pre-rollout checklist for model version or config change:
  1. Capacity runbook updated with expected memory/latency/cpu/GPU usage.
  2. Canary plan: route 1-5% traffic to canary for 24-72h.
  3. Load test plan (k6/vegeta) executed against canary at 1.5-2x expected peak.
  4. Error budget check: ensure SLOs are within Green before moving to global rollout.

Sizing and Right-sizing
- Use traffic distribution percentiles (p50, p95, p99) and per-request resource profiles to model capacity needs.
- For GPU-backed services, maintain mixed-quantization profiles and autoscaling thresholds to trade latency vs cost.
- Scheduled maintenance windows must be included in capacity forecasts and customer notifications.

3) Reliability Initiatives and Investment Prioritization

Initiative Types
- Reactive: follow-ups from postmortems and large incidents.
- Proactive: capacity automation, improved observability, chaos experiments, and reliability-focused refactors.

Prioritization Criteria
- Impact to SLOs / number of customers affected.
- Probability of recurrence and cost to mitigate.
- Operational overhead reduction and automation potential.

Example Initiative Roadmap (quarterly)
- Q1: Automated cold-start cache for frequent prompts (reduce p95 cold-start latency by 40%).
- Q2: Autoscaler improvements to reduce scale-up time under sudden bursts (target: 50% faster spin-up).
- Q3: Model routing fallback logic to enable degraded-but-functional inference on capacity limits.

4) Incident Review Standards and Postmortems

Blameless Culture
- Reviews are blameless: focus on systemic improvements rather than individual fault.
- Encourage psychological safety — authoring a postmortem is expected and rewarded.

Postmortem Requirements (mandatory for Sev 2+ incidents or >1 hour user-impacting outages)
- Executive summary (2-3 sentences).
- Timeline (UTC timestamps): detection -> mitigation -> recovery -> close.
- Impact statement: affected customers, API routes, and estimated user minutes lost.
- Root cause analysis (RCA): include causal chain and evidence (logs, traces, metrics).
- Action items: owner, due date, status. At least one action should be preventative and trackable.
- Lessons learned and follow-ups.

Postmortem Review Process
1. Draft postmortem within 72 hours.
2. Triage meeting with SRE, service owner, and product to validate facts within 7 days.
3. Publish final postmortem to Confluence and link to incident ticket.
4. Assign action items and track until complete.

Incident Metrics to Collect
- Mean Time To Detect (MTTD), Mean Time To Mitigate (MTTM), Mean Time To Recover (MTTR).
- Error budget consumed during the incident window.
- Number of paged responders and escalations.

5) Operational Tooling Expectations

Standard Tooling Stack (approved)
- Observability: Datadog (metrics + dashboards), Honeycomb/Tempo for traces.
- Logging: ELK stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) with 30d retention for infra logs.
- Alerting & On-call: PagerDuty for paging, Slack for incident channels, JIRA for incident tickets.
- Runbook storage & CI: Confluence for canonical runbooks, GitHub repo infra/runbooks for versioning and PR-based edits.

Dashboards and Alerts
- Each SLO must have an associated dashboard and a burn-rate alert. Create dashboards per region/model-version.
- Alert tuning: avoid noisy alerts — alerts should fire for actionable thresholds only. Use multi-stage notification (pager for high-severity, slack for info).

Runbook Requirements
- Runbooks must be concise, action-oriented, and executable from the CLI when possible. Include:
  - Purpose and scope.
  - Pre-reqs (permissions, tools).
  - Quick detection queries (Datadog/PromQL).
  - Immediate mitigation steps with exact commands.
  - Rollback and mitigation verification.
  - Post-incident cleanup.
  - Contacts & escalation matrix.

Tooling Automation
- SLO monitoring automation (infra/slo-monitor) should create JIRA tickets and add context links when thresholds hit.
- Continuous runbook validation: periodically run smoke remediation scripts in a non-prod environment to validate steps.

6) Canonical SRE Runbook Template (required fields)
Title: short descriptive name (e.g., infer-service-high-latency)
Service: service name and team
Scope: what this runbook covers
Detection queries: sample queries and dashboards
Impact indicators: what constitutes low/medium/high impact
Immediate mitigation (fast actions): numbered steps to reduce user impact (time-sensitive)
Root-cause investigation: longer diagnostic commands and queries
Rollback procedures: safe rollback steps with verification
Post-incident tasks: cleanup, follow-ups, and ticketing
Contacts: on-call, owners, escalation emails, Slack channels
Runbook example: infer-service-high-latency
- Service: inference-runtime / runtime-team
- Scope: High tail latency (>p99) for text generation routes across a region
- Detection queries:
  - Datadog: `avg(last_5m):percentile(99,trace.http.request.duration){service:inference-runtime,route:generate} > 700`
  - Traces: search for requests with duration > 700ms and inspect kernel scheduling + queue wait spans
- Immediate mitigation (fast actions):
  1. Check autoscaler status: `kubectl -n inference get hpa` and `kubectl -n inference describe hpa inference-runtime`
  2. If autoscaler is saturated, increase replica count to safe max: `kubectl -n inference scale deployment/inference-runtime --replicas=10` (replace 10 with region safe max in capacity dashboard)
  3. Throttle non-critical routes: update gateway rate-limits for low-priority routes (example command in rate-limit service repo)
  4. Enable degraded model routing (fallback): `curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/feature-flags/fallback?enable=true &service=inference-runtime`
  5. Notify channel #inc-inference and page on-call if sustained after step 2.
- Investigation:
  - Check GPU utilization: `kubectl -n inference top pods` and cluster-level GPU metrics dashboard.
  - Inspect queue lengths and batching latencies (metrics: batch.queue_length, batch.latency_p50/p95/p99).
  - Correlate with recent deploys: `git log --since=24.hours --pretty=oneline infra/deploys` and check rollout timeline.
- Rollback (if caused by recent deploy):
  1. Initiate standardized rollback: `ops-cli rollback --service inference-runtime --to-tag <previous-tag>`
  2. Verify SLOs return to Green for p99 within 30m of rollback.
- Post-incident cleanup: revert temporary throttles, disable fallback only after SLOs stable for 2h, document in incident ticket.
- Contacts: runtime-team on-call rota, runtime-team@redwood.internal, #inc-inference on Slack.

7) Governance, Training, and Continuous Improvement

Governance
- SRE team owns the standards and periodic reviews. All changes to this doc must go through an SRE-approved PR.
- Quarterly audit: check that every production service has published SLOs, a runbook, and a recent postmortem (if there was a Sev2+ incident).

Training
- On-call onboarding: 1-week on-call bootcamp with runbook exercises and simulated pagers.
- Game days: biannual game days focused on capacity failover and large-scale rollbacks.

Continuous Improvement
- Maintain an issues backlog for reliability investments and track via product OKRs.
- Use metrics (MTTR, MTTD, error budget burn) to measure progress and adjust priorities.

Appendices
A. Example SLO registry entry (YAML snippet)
```
name: inference-p99-latency
service: inference-runtime
sli: "trace.http.request.duration{route:generate,service:inference-runtime}"
target: 0.995
window: 30d
alert_thresholds:
  burn_rate: 14d:yellow,7d:red
owner: runtime-team@redwood.internal
```

B. Escalation matrix (summary)
- Tier 1: Service on-call (15 minutes) -> runtime-team@redwood.internal
- Tier 2: SRE lead (30 minutes) -> sre-leads@redwood.internal
- Tier 3: Engineering manager + product (60 minutes) -> eng-managers@redwood.internal

C. Useful links
- SLO registry: https://github.com/redwood/infra/slo-registry
- Runbook repo: https://github.com/redwood/infra/runbooks
- Incident ticket template: https://redwood.atlassian.net/servicedesk/INCIDENT-TEMPLATE
- Observability dashboards: Datadog > Redwood > inference-runtime

If you are the service owner and anything in this document is unclear, please contact the SRE team (sre-team@redwood.internal).
